title: DeepSeek Web Search API Agents: Cost and Setup (2026)
summary: DeepSeek Web Search API agents let your code search and fetch web pages. You'll know how to configure them, what rate limits apply, and how to fix errors.
body_markdown:
## Run the DeepSeek agent as a step in an Activepieces workflow


From a schedule, form or webhook,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/deepseek) can start the DeepSeek call and send the result to a sheet or Slack, two of its 742 integrations. The iteration cap then lives in one place instead of in a loop nobody is watching.


### Use your own DeepSeek provider key


Activepieces works with any major model or your own provider key, so DeepSeek spend can land on your own account. Its catalog also lists a DeepSeek integration,` @activepieces/piece-deepseek` , with a single action.


Nothing I can point at shows that either one wraps DeepSeek's search-and-fetch endpoints. Treat both as model access, and check the integration's action list before assuming it can search.


Once the DeepSeek integration is connected in Activepieces, an agent can call it: the same action that runs as a flow step is exposed as a tool on the project's MCP server, which Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent of your own can reach.


There is no second catalog to publish to, so the DeepSeek call is wired once, not twice.


Every connector is an agent tool, all 742 of them counted in the MIT-licensed open source repo, where the mechanism sits in` packages/pieces` ; MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production, and we haven't run this particular call ourselves.


### Build a workflow that searches on a schedule


Start with a Schedule trigger. The builder shows it as "1. Every Hour", with an option to skip weekends and a sample-data panel that reads "Tested Successfully" once the trigger fires.


That last status matters: a trigger that hasn't produced sample data gives later steps nothing to map, so test it before you add anything.


After that, the next-step picker offers a spreadsheet action such as Insert Row under Google Sheets.


Add your DeepSeek call between the trigger and that row. Hold the query and the iteration cap as fixed values in the flow, and write failures to the sheet as rows too, so a bad hour shows up as a row and not as silence.


With a form or webhook trigger the setup is the same. The difference is that a person or another system decides when the call runs, so repeated submissions can drive repeated calls.


### When to call the API directly instead


If the integration's single action doesn't expose the search and fetch parameters you need, use the generic HTTP step against DeepSeek's documented endpoint.


That's also the right route when you need to read raw error bodies and branch on them, because a wrapper may flatten them into one failure.


Keep the trigger and the sheet or Slack delivery in Activepieces, where flows are unlimited on every plan including free, and let the HTTP step carry the request you validated first.
